3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 8 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying material allegations and stating that the suit property originally belonged to their predecessor Alabuddin who took lease of the same from the landlord on tile basis of kabuliyat and patta from the landlord Gouri Pria Debi at an annual jama of Taka 16.00 and as the taluk of Gouripria Debi was purchased by Nabin Chandra Chakraborty said Alabuddin executed a kabuliyat in favour of the purchaser landlord who also executed a paua in his favour on 24th Kartick, 1310 BS Ext. 'A'. Since then Alabuddin was in possession of the entire suit property. Further case of the defendants was that the said Alabuddin had a brother named Sona Guzi who married mother of plaintiffs predecessor Rahmat Ali who came to the house of Sona Gazi and after the death of Sonagazi and his 2nd wife out of compassion Alabuddin allowed Rahmat Ali to possess the Suit plot Nos.160, 224 and 226. Taking advantage of old age and ignorance of Alabuddin the said Rahmat Ali during the CS operation wrongly recorded 0.08 annas share of the suit land in the suit khatian though he had no title in the suit property. Further case of the contesting defendants is that Yusuf Ali and Jinnat Ali, two sons of Alabuddin while in title and possession of the suit land executed a confirmatory kabuliyat in favour of landlord, Nabin Chakraborty on 4th Agrahayan 1331 BS and got a paua on the same date from the said landlord Ext. A(1) and since then they are in possession of the entire suit land except those three suit plots on payment of rents from before CS khatian in the name of Alabuddin and his heirs vide Ext. 'B' series. Their further case is that sons of Rahmat Ali relinquished possession of plot Nos. 224 and 226 in favour of Ishab Ali and Jinnat Ali after taking settlement of some land from them by a kabuliyat dated 3rd Chaitra, 1330 BS Ext. C. Their further case is that Alabuddin and after his death his heirs paid rent of the suit property to the landlord. 

 6. It appears that trial Court found that Alabuddin had 8 annas share and Rahmat Ali had 8 annas share in the suit tenancy although the original patta stood in the name of Alabuddin alone and that Rahmat Ali was in possession of about half of the tenancy. On the other hand Court of appeal below found that Alabuddin took lease on his own behalf and on behalf of his nephew Rahmat Ali and the plaintiffs have possession in the suit land. But none, of the Courts below found in which suit plots plaintiffs have exclusive or joint possession. It is not denied that only plot Nos. 160, 224 and 226 having an area of 50 acres were recorded in exclusive possession of plaintiffs' predecessor Rahmat Ali in the CS khatian Ext. 2 and other 10 plots except homestead plot No. 224 were recorded in exclusive possession of defendants predeceassor Alabuddin in the said khatian. Though the plaintiffs stated in para 7 of the plaint that Alabuddin and Rahmat Ali possessed the suit land in equal share and entry regarding exclusive possession in the CS khatian was wrong they did not state in which other plots they had possession. Plaintiffs adduced evidence to the effect that before compromise they possessed 7/8 plots and after compromise they possess 5 plots but none of the PWs could say in which plots plaintiffs possessed before compromise. Trial Court without considering the presumption of entry regarding possession in the CS khatian, failure of the PWs to state the plot numbers in which plaintiffs had possession and reliability of the PWs erroneously opined that plaintiffs previously possessed 7/8 plots. If the entry in the CS khatian Ext. 2 regarding share of plaintiffs' predecessor Rahmat Ali and defendants' predecessor Alabuddin is found to be correct the entry regarding exclusive possession of the said two persons cannot be found to be incorrect. As a matter of fact none of the Courts below specifically found the said entry regarding exclusive possession in the said CS khatian to be wrong or incorrect. I do not find any illegality in the finding of the Courts below regarding share of the parties in the suit property as recorded in the CS khatian inasmuch as both the Courts below considered the patta Ext. A and rent receipts Ext. B series in the name of Alabuddin along with other evidence on record for arriving at the said finding. But I fail to agree with the finding of the Courts below regarding possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land as the same suffers from non-consideration of material evidence on record and presumption arising from entry in the CS Khatian.
